correctness.rationale: Extraspecial G has G/G′=C_p^(2n), hence p^(2n) linear characters, one principal (codegree1) and p^(2n)-1 nonprincipal (codegree p). Its p-1 nonlinear degree-p^n characters are indexed by faithful nontrivial center characters; they vanish off the center so are faithful and have codegree p^(n+1). The degree-squared sum p^(2n)+(p-1)p^(2n)=p^(2n+1) exhausts Irr(G). Least nontrivial and largest codegrees recover p,n. The two extraspecial isomorphism types have identical data. Independent arithmetic checks across 25 (prime,rank) pairs match.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A negative global rigidity theorem does not subsume a positive internal classification. Nor does an abelian comparison theorem distinguish the two extraspecial types.

originality.rationale: The character table of an extraspecial group is classical and fully credited. Moretó introduced pseudo-algebras and Lewis–Yan give non-rigidity of group order in general, but the latter full 2024 paper proves comparisons with particular abelian groups, not the exact extraspecial-family invariant. The new statement is exact codegree multiplicities and within-family order/type classification, subject to possible older codegree-table equivalents.
residual_risks: An older character-codegree multiplicity computation might contain the same three-pair invariant without term pseudo-algebra.
The comparison guarantees order only if both groups are known extraspecial; no claim for arbitrary same-invariant group.

value.rationale: Group pseudo-algebra rigidity is an explicit motivating invariant question. Extraspecial groups are a canonical two-type family in all prime ranks; a uniform exact formula determines which information the invariant preserves and loses. Though the derivation from known character tables is short, it supplies a complete motivated restricted-family answer, not only a relabelled character-degree count.

limitations: An older character-codegree multiplicity computation might contain the same three-pair invariant without term pseudo-algebra.
The comparison guarantees order only if both groups are known extraspecial; no claim for arbitrary same-invariant group.
